input.title: ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX
input.bodyText:
ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX
Prepared by Julia Lawson (Product), 1 October 2025. Written for Zombie Match 3D as the game is today. If the core gameplay changes during the pause, we will redo the affected parts of this brief with you in November.

1. Start date
Project start (kickoff) is Monday 3 November 2025. The asset hand-off list linked at the end shows what we have already sent you, what is ready to send, and what we still owe before that date.

2. Scenario and what it is for
We picked Scenario 1, the core gameplay. The playable should show the game in its simplest and most authentic form: drag items into the tray, make matches of three, and the matched items are thrown at the zombies. It is meant to filter for players who will like the real game, not to chase the cheapest install. So it should stay true to the core loop rather than turn into a mini-game. Different items hit differently (for example, the grenade is powerful, the couch does splash damage and the plushies are weak but funny), and the playable should get that across.

3. Board: the eight items
These eight items go on the board by default:
- Grenade
- Couch
- Plushie Chick (the "duck" in the reference level)
- Shuriken
- Cute Axe
- Gift Box
- Cactus Plant
- Bow
Every other board item on the hand-off list is an extra. You can swap extras in, and we would like to be able to test them on the board, as you offered. Note: the Bow replaces Dynamite from the earlier list. Dynamite is now an extra.

4. Zombies and animation
- Four zombies: Party Girl, Plumber, Magician, Football Player. All four are in the Unity zombie pack Marcus put together, which you already have.
- One animation: walk.
We may add more zombies at a later stage, depending on scope and size.

5. How a level plays (from the ZM3D design page and our reference level)
- Items sit in a physics pile on the board. The player drags items into the tray. Any three matching items clear from the tray and are fired at the zombies.
- The tray has 7 slots.
- Win: every zombie on screen is eliminated.
- Lose: the zombies reach us and our HP runs out.
- Filling all 7 slots without a match is a blunder, not a loss. The tray clears, the surviving zombies enrage, and play continues. The loss screen only appears when HP reaches zero.
- The cannon on the pack list is what you called the rocket launcher. It went out with its projectile. The background is the one from the reference level.
- Reference: our reference-level deck ("ZM3D playable - reference level") and Brian's recording of the level from 24 September.

6. Sound and music
- Sound: we only hand over sounds that are ours to hand over. Anything from a sound library or a bought pack stays with us until we have our own version. The hand-off list shows which sound files are coming.
- Music: as you set out on our last playable, the music may only start after the player's first tap or click. It must not autoplay when the playable loads. The background music is a loop we are still cutting down from our ad track.

7. Formats
As you told us, and these still hold:
- 3D assets: .fbx, .glb or .blend. FBX must be exported in Binary format, not ASCII.
- 2D assets: .png. For 2D animations, character parts must be separated into pieces.
- Font: .ttf or .woff2
- Sound: .mp3 or .wav

8. What is still coming from us
The hand-off list (a Google Sheet shared alongside this doc) has one row per line of our pack list, with its state:
- Delivered: you already have the current file.
- Ready: exported in a format you accept, in our outgoing folder, opens, current, and not being changed.
- Owed: still to come. The row says what is owed and who on our side has the next step.
Contacts on our side: Frederick Stone (project lead), Julia Lawson (product), Brian Foster (asset pack), Robert (game design).

input.message:
Done. The brief and the hand-off list are both in my Drive. They're shared view-only with you, Brian, Robert and PlayableX intake, and both links are posted in the PlayableX channel.
• Brief: https://docs.google.com/document/d/02e99d3308671f82855cd925/edit
• Hand-off list: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1lN8xKJqvlIKrF5cGzXsQRFtQD9EHrSM-VE2HI_34cM4/edit

Counts across Brian's 96 pack lines:
• *Delivered: 8*
• *Ready: 58*
• *Owed: 30*

What's behind the Owed count:
• 12 kitchen and living-room models Brian saved out of Unity on 25 Sep are ASCII FBX (Marcus flagged it on the 26th). PlayableX only take binary, so Brian has to re-export them.
• Chainsaw, Cone and Cactus Plant changed in Claire's PR #462 after her FBXs went out, so they need re-exporting by Claire. Cactus Plant is one of the default eight.
• 11 models still haven't been exported (6 waiting on Claire, 5 Brian's), plus the music loop (Calvin), item icons and UI PNGs (Brian), and fonts (Martin).
Robert swapped the Bow in for Dynamite on 26 Sep, so the board eight now include the Bow. The 30 Owed tickets are in Todo, each with a comment saying what's owed and who has it.

Hi <@PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID>, ahead of the 3 November start, here are the two documents for the Zombie Match 3D playable:
• *Brief* (scenario, the 8 board items, the 4 zombies with the walk animation, win/lose rules, the 7-slot tray, sound and music, formats): https://docs.google.com/document/d/02e99d3308671f82855cd925/edit
• *Hand-off list*: one row per asset, showing what you already have (Delivered), what's exported and waiting in our outgoing folder (Ready), and what's still coming from us (Owed): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1lN8xKJqvlIKrF5cGzXsQRFtQD9EHrSM-VE2HI_34cM4/edit
Both are shared with your intake address. The brief describes the game as it is today. If the core gameplay changes during the pause, we'll redo the affected parts with you in November.
